blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing freight and carriers well means treating carriers as partners with a real performance history, not as a list of prices you call when you need a truck. The best logistics teams score their carriers every month on a small, consistent set of metrics: on-time pickup, on-time delivery, damage rate, and responsiveness when something goes wrong.

A good carrier scorecard is shared with the carriers themselves. The ones that are doing well see it and feel recognised. The ones that are slipping see it and have a clear chance to correct before anyone starts a harder conversation.

Over a year, this quiet discipline builds a core of reliable carriers that know your operation, trust your team, and answer the phone at 6 a.m. when you really need them.

items.q: How does the text say carriers should be treated?
options: As a list of prices to call when you need a truck
As partners with a real performance history
items.why: "treating carriers as partners with a real performance history, not as a list of prices".

items.q: Which metrics does the text mention for the monthly scorecard?
options: On-time pickup, on-time delivery, damage rate and responsiveness
Fuel cost, mileage and driver age
items.why: O texto lista exatamente essas quatro métricas.

items.q: Why does the text say the scorecard is SHARED with the carriers?
options: So strong carriers feel recognised and weaker ones can correct early
To compare them publicly with competitors
To force them to lower their prices
items.why: "feel recognised… have a clear chance to correct before anyone starts a harder conversation".

items.q: The phrase "before anyone starts a harder conversation" SUGGESTS that…
options: carriers are usually fired without warning
the team dislikes talking to carriers
sharing data early is meant to avoid the need for confrontation later
items.why: Inferência: o feedback antecipado dá chance de corrigir e evita o confronto posterior.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Reliability is worth more than a single low quote
The cheapest carrier available should always win the load
Consistent metrics build trust over time
Carriers respond better when they can see their own numbers
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta contra escolher só pelo preço — valoriza histórico e confiabilidade.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando o novo cartão de desempenho à equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Morning, everyone. Before we assign a single load today, I want to walk you through something new. Starting this month, we have a carrier scorecard — one page, four numbers per carrier. On-time pickup, on-time delivery, damage rate, and how fast they respond when a load goes wrong.

I know how this desk has worked for years: whoever answers the phone fastest gets the freight. That has kept us moving, and I'm grateful for it. But it has also let a couple of carriers slip badly without any of us really noticing, because nobody was writing it down.

Here's what changes. Every carrier gets their own scorecard, and we send it to them. The ones that have delivered for us all year will see that we've noticed. The ones that are slipping get an honest number and a fair chance to fix it before we move their loads elsewhere.

This isn't about punishing anyone. It's about building a core of carriers we can trust at six in the morning. Give it three months. I'm confident the phone will still get answered — just by the right people.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Harry introducing to the team?
options: A one-page carrier scorecard with four metrics
items.why: "we have a carrier scorecard — one page, four numbers per carrier."

items.q: How does Harry describe how the desk has worked so far?
options: A manager assigned every load personally
Whoever answers the phone fastest gets the freight
items.why: "whoever answers the phone fastest gets the freight."

items.q: What problem does Harry say the old method caused?
options: The team lost too many phone calls
Some carriers slipped badly without anyone noticing
items.why: "it has also let a couple of carriers slip badly without any of us really noticing."

items.q: When Harry says "This isn't about punishing anyone," he most likely wants to…
options: reassure the team that the scorecard is fair, not a threat
cancel the whole plan if people object
warn the carriers they will be replaced
avoid sharing the data with carriers
items.why: Inferência: ele antecipa a resistência e enquadra o placar como justiça, não punição.

items.q: What does Harry expect after three months?
options: That the team will stop answering the phone
That the scorecard will be dropped
That the phone will still get answered, but by the right carriers
items.why: "the phone will still get answered — just by the right people."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We only book reliable carriers for the overnight runs." Reliable means…
options: that you can consistently count on
items.why: Reliable = confiável, com quem se pode contar de forma consistente.

items.q: "Two of our carriers have started to slip this quarter." To slip here means to…
items.why: To slip = perder desempenho, cair de nível.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We score every carrier on a carrier ___ each month: pickup, delivery, damage and response."
items.why: Scorecard = cartão de desempenho, onde as métricas são registradas.

items.q: "Their responsiveness is what saved that shipment." Responsiveness is…
options: how quickly they react when something goes wrong
items.why: Responsiveness = responsividade, a rapidez em reagir a um problema.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We judge a carrier by its whole ___, not by one good week."
items.why: Performance history = histórico de desempenho, o registro ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns na gestão de transportadoras. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We're going to roll out the scorecard across all lanes next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The RH team still has to sign off on the new carrier list." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "A few dispatchers pushed back on the idea at first." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They promised improvements but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Chasing the cheapest quote won't move the needle on reliability." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
